meta.title: UGC NET Banking/Financial Sector PYQs (June 2019 - June 2025)
meta.source_note: Transcribed from scanned previous-year question paper photos (compiled by a coaching provider, e.g. Adda247-style compilation). These are recycled exam questions, not original content owned by the compiler.
meta.data_quality_note: Questions flagged 'ocr_incomplete': true have uncertain stems, options, and/or answers due to low scan resolution or faint print. Their 'answer' field may be null or a best-effort guess explained in 'note'. All flagged items should be verified against an official answer key before use in study/quiz material.

fields.q_no: Question number (1-147), sequential across all exam sessions in this set
fields.exam_session: The UGC NET exam session this question appeared in
fields.question_type: Format of the question (Simple MCQ, Multi-Select, Matching, Sequencing, Chronological Sequencing, Assertion-Reason, Statement-based True/False)
fields.question: The question text
fields.answer: Correct option letter, or null if unconfirmed
fields.note: Explanation/reasoning for the answer, or a flag about transcription uncertainty
fields.ocr_incomplete: true if the source scan was too degraded to transcribe with full confidence

questions.question: Arrange the following in chronological order of the milestones achieved by the National Stock Exchange of India: A. Commencement of Trading in Index options B. Launch of Securities Lending and Borrowing Scheme C. Commencement of Derivatives Trading in Index Futures D. Launch of Mutual Fund Service System E. Launch of S&P CNX Nifty
questions.note: Per the printed solution: Launch of S&P CNX Nifty (1996) -> Commencement of Derivatives Trading in Index Futures (2000) -> Commencement of Trading in Index Options (2001) -> Launch of Mutual Fund Service System (2009) -> Launch of Securities Lending and Borrowing Scheme (2012).

questions.question: A term loan becomes Non Performing Asset (NPA) if its interest and/or installment of principal remains overdue for a period of more than:
questions.note: Confirmed by printed solution: RBI norms classify a loan as NPA once interest/principal is overdue for more than 90 days.

questions.question: In which year did the State Bank of India come into existence?
questions.note: SBI was constituted on 1 July 1955 under the SBI Act, 1955 (from the Imperial Bank of India).

questions.question: Match the LIST-I (Term) with LIST-II (Explanation): A. Nostro Account, B. Vostro Account, C. Bid, D. Offer / I. Account held by a foreign bank with a local bank, II. An Indian Bank's Swiss Franc A/C with a bank in Switzerland, III. Price at which the dealer is willing to buy another currency, IV. Price at which the dealer is willing to sell another currency

list_2.I: Account held by a foreign bank with a local bank
list_2.II: An Indian Bank's Swiss Franc A/C with a bank in Switzerland
list_2.III: Price at which the dealer is willing to buy another currency
list_2.IV: Price at which the dealer is willing to sell another currency

questions.note: Nostro = 'our account with you' (domestic bank's foreign-currency account abroad, e.g. an Indian bank's account in Switzerland) = II; Vostro = 'your account with us' (a foreign bank's account with the local bank) = I; Bid = price dealer will buy at = III; Offer = price dealer will sell at = IV.

questions.question: In which of the following years was the Investor Protection and Education Fund Regulations issued by the Securities and Exchange Board of India?
questions.note: SEBI (Investor Protection and Education Fund) Regulations were notified in 2009.

questions.question: An unsecured short-term promissory note, negotiable and transferable by endorsement and delivery, with a fixed maturity period, issued at a discount by creditworthy corporates, primary dealers, and all-India financial institutions is known as:
questions.note: This is the standard textbook definition of Commercial Paper.

questions.question: Arrange the following Development Financial Institutions in chronological order of their establishment (Old to New): A. IFCI B. IDBI C. NABARD D. SIDBI
questions.note: IFCI: 1948, IDBI: 1964, NABARD: 1982, SIDBI: 1990 -> chronological old-to-new is A,B,C,D.

questions.question: Which one of the following is a value-added service of EXIM Bank?
questions.note: Options and exact answer are not fully legible in the scan; verify against official key.

questions.question: Arrange the following institutions in ascending order of their year of establishment: A. SEBI B. Reserve Bank of India C. State Bank of India D. NABARD E. NHB
questions.note: RBI: 1935, SBI: 1955, NABARD: 1982, NHB: 1988, SEBI (statutory): 1992 -> B,C,D,E,A. Exact option lettering in the scan is faint; verify.

questions.question: Match the Financial Inclusion Yojanas with their respective years of launch: A. PM Jan Dhan B. PM Mudra C. Stand Up India D. Vaya Vandana / I. 2016 II. 2014 III. 2017 IV. 2015
questions.note: PM Jan Dhan Yojana: 2014, PM Mudra Yojana: 2015, Stand Up India: 2016, Pradhan Mantri Vaya Vandana Yojana: 2017.

questions.question: Which one of the following conditions is NOT true as per the IRDA Act, 1999 for entry of private players into the insurance market?

options.a: The company's sole purpose is to carry on life insurance business or general insurance business or reinsurance business
options.b: The minimum paid-up equity capital for life insurance or general insurance business is Rs. 100 crore
options.c: The minimum paid-up capital for carrying reinsurance business is Rs. 200 crore
options.d: Insurance companies are required to invest not less than 15 percent of their funds in infrastructure and social sectors

questions.note: Text is partly faint in the scan; the false statement (answer) could not be confirmed with confidence. Verify against official key.

questions.question: Which of the following are the features of Treasury Bills? A. Negotiable Securities B. Issued at par and are repaid at premium on maturity C. High liquidity on account of short tenure D. Assured Yield E. High transaction cost
questions.note: T-Bills are negotiable, issued at a discount (not premium) and repaid at par, highly liquid, and carry assured yield; low transaction cost -> A,C,D fit best.

questions.question: The Securities Exchange Board of India (SEBI) regulates and supervises the securities market through:
questions.note: Options list is faint (A. Regulations B. Rules C. Guidelines D. Orders) and answer combination not confirmed; verify.

questions.question: Arrange the following SEBI regulations in the ascending year of their enactment: A. RDR regulations B. Intermediaries regulations C. Real estate investment trust regulations D. Buy-Back of Securities by listed companies regulations E. Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements Regulations
questions.note: Option lettering is not fully legible in the scan; verify against official key.

questions.question: Which one of the following is the development role of RBI?

options.a: Formulates, implements, and monitors the monetary policy
options.b: Prescribes broad parameters of banking operations
options.c: Issues, exchanges, and destroys currency notes
options.d: Performs a wide range of promotional functions to support national objectives

questions.note: RBI's developmental role (as distinct from its regulatory/monetary functions) is described as performing promotional functions supporting national objectives.

questions.question: The Capital Adequacy Ratio (CAR) for Indian Public Sector banks set by RBI is:
questions.note: RBI mandates a minimum CAR of 9% under Basel norms, but Indian PSU banks are required to maintain 12% (higher than the regulatory minimum) per government policy — this option combination is uncertain from the scan; verify.

questions.question: Arrange the following banks in the increasing order of their year of formation: A. State Bank of India B. Imperial Bank of India C. Reserve Bank of India D. Regional Rural Banks E. Small Finance Bank
questions.note: Imperial Bank of India: 1921, RBI: 1935, SBI: 1955, RRBs: 1975, Small Finance Banks: 2015 -> order B,C,A,D,E.

questions.question: Match the columns: List-I Institutions: A. National Housing Bank B. Industrial Development Bank of India C. Small Industrial Development Bank of India D. Industrial Finance Corporation of India / List-II Date of establishment: I. 01-07-1964 II. 01-07-1948 III. 02-04-1990 IV. 09-07-1988

list_1.C: Small Industrial Development Bank of India

questions.note: NHB established 1988, IDBI 1964, SIDBI 1990, IFCI 1948 -> A-IV, B-I, C-III, D-II.

questions.question: Which of the following subsidiaries are fully owned by the Reserve Bank of India? A. National Housing Bank B. National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development C. The Deposit Insurance and Credit Guarantee Corporation of India D. Bhartiya Reserve Bank Note Mudran Private Limited E. Securities Trading Corporation of India
questions.note: DICGC and BRBNMPL are wholly owned RBI subsidiaries; NHB's ownership was transferred to the Government in 2019 (previously RBI-owned).

questions.question: Which one of the following is a Value Added Service of EXIM Bank?
Which of the following are the instruments of qualitative Credit Control Methods in India's Monetary Policy?
questions.note: This is a multi-select statement question (choose the correct combination) — the combination options (a)-(d) with letter groupings were not legible in the scan; qualitative tools are Consumer Credit Regulation, Margin Requirements and Differential/Direct interest rate action (B, C, E), while CRR and SLR are quantitative tools.

questions.question: The Narasimham Committee 1991 recommended reforms with respect to the banking sector. These reforms are also known as:
questions.note: The Narasimham Committee-I (1991) reforms are generally referred to as financial sector reforms.

questions.question: SEBI permitted the issue of commercial papers within the framework of its guidelines. Which one of the following committees recommended these guidelines?
questions.note: The Vaghul Working Group (1987) recommended introduction of Commercial Paper in India.

questions.question: Which of the following are primary functions of Commercial Banks? A. Accepting Deposits B. Agency Service C. Discounting Trade Bills D. Financing Foreign Trade E. General Utility Service
questions.note: Accepting deposits, discounting trade bills, and financing foreign trade are all forms of the core banking function (deposits/lending); agency and general utility services are secondary functions.

questions.question: Which of the following are the participants in T-Bills Market? A. Reserve Bank of India B. Commercial Banks C. Foreign Banks D. Provident Funds E. Corporates
questions.note: RBI, commercial banks, foreign banks, provident funds, and corporates/institutions all participate in the T-Bills market.

questions.question: Which of the following are different types of dumping? A. Persistent Dumping B. Predatory Dumping C. Sporadic Dumping D. Nomadic Dumping
questions.note: The recognised types of dumping are Persistent, Predatory, and Sporadic dumping; 'Nomadic dumping' is not a standard category.

questions.question: Match List-I with List-II: List-I Instruments: A. Forwards B. Certificate of Deposits C. FPO D. IPO / List-II Market: I. Primary Market II. Money Market III. Derivative Market IV. Stock Market
questions.note: Forwards trade in the derivatives market (III), Certificates of Deposit in the money market (II), FPO happens in the primary market (I), and post-IPO shares trade on the stock market (IV).

questions.question: Which of the following are the schemes promoted by NABARD? A. Kisan Credit Card (KCC) B. Capital Investment Subsidy Scheme C. Special Economic Zone Scheme D. Rural Innovation Fund E. Tribal Development Fund
questions.note: NABARD promotes KCC, Capital Investment Subsidy Scheme, Rural Innovation Fund, and Tribal Development Fund; Special Economic Zones are not a NABARD scheme.

questions.question: In which of the following ratios is the share capital of RRBs prescribed for the Central Government, State Government, and Sponsoring bank?
questions.note: RRB share capital is held by Central Government, State Government, and the sponsor bank in the ratio 50:15:35.

questions.question: Match List-I with List-II: List-I Institution: A. Industrial Finance Corporation of India (IFCI) B. Industrial Development Bank of India (IDBI) C. Industrial Credit and Investment Corporation of India (ICICI) D. India Infrastructure Finance Company Limited (IIFCL) / List-II Year of establishment: I. 2006 II. 1964 III. 1955 IV. 1948

list_1.C: Industrial Credit and Investment Corporation of India (ICICI)

questions.note: IFCI: 1948, IDBI: 1964, ICICI: 1955, IIFCL: 2006 -> A-IV, B-II, C-III, D-I.

questions.question: In which type of insurance should insurable interest be present at the time when the policy is taken?
questions.note: For life insurance, insurable interest must exist at the time the policy is taken (not necessarily at the time of claim); for fire insurance it's needed at inception and at loss, for marine insurance it's needed at the time of loss (can be acquired after the policy is taken).

questions.question: Which of the following Statements are correct about Regional Rural Banks? A. The first RRB's were established on October 02, 1975 B. The RRB's Act of 1976 is applicable C. The minimum paid up capital of RRB's is 10 crores D. The Service of RRB's are not available in the state of Goa and Sikkim E. RRB's are owned by Central Government, State governments and the sponsor bank in the proportion of 50%, 15% and 35%
questions.note: First RRBs began 2 Oct 1975; governed by the RRB Act, 1976; not present in Goa and Sikkim; ownership ratio is 50:15:35 (Centre:State:Sponsor bank).

questions.question: Arrange the following financial institutions according to their year of establishment, from earlier to later: A. Imperial Bank B. State Bank of India C. Life Insurance Corporation of India D. Unit Trust of India E. Regional Rural Banks
questions.note: Imperial Bank of India: 1921, SBI: 1955, LIC: 1956, UTI: 1964, RRBs: 1975.

questions.question: The minimum capital prescribed by the RBI for starting a new small finance bank is:
questions.note: RBI's revised (2019) guidelines set minimum paid-up capital for a Small Finance Bank at Rs. 200 crore.

questions.question: The system where two or more banking companies are controlled by one or two individuals is called:
questions.note: Chain banking is where control of two or more independently chartered banks is held by a small group of individuals.

questions.question: Which of the following are quantitative credit control methods? A. Bank Rate Policy B. Open market Operations C. Rationing of credit D. Margin requirements E. Variable reserve ratio
questions.note: Bank rate, open market operations, and variable reserve ratio (CRR/SLR) are quantitative tools; margin requirements and credit rationing are selective/qualitative tools.

questions.question: A committee was set up in 1993 under the chairmanship of R.N. Malhotra to evaluate which of the following?
questions.note: The Malhotra Committee (1993) was constituted to recommend reforms in the Indian insurance sector.

questions.question: Match List-I with List-II: List-I Institution: A. Industrial Finance Corporation of India (IFCI) B. Industrial Development Bank of India (IDBI) C. Industrial Credit and Investment Corporation of India (ICICI) D. India Infrastructure Finance Company Limited (IIFCL) / List-II Year of establishment: I. 1948 II. 1964 III. 1955 IV. 2006

list_1.C: Industrial Credit and Investment Corporation of India (ICICI)

questions.note: IFCI: 1948, IDBI: 1964, ICICI: 1955, IIFCL: 2006 -> A-I, B-II, C-III, D-IV.

questions.question: Arrange the following financial institutions according to the order in which they were established: A. NABARD B. NHB C. EXIM Bank D. SIDBI
questions.note: EXIM Bank: Jan 1982, NABARD: Jul 1982, NHB: 1988, SIDBI: 1990 -> C,A,B,D.

questions.question: Arrange the following Regional Rural Banks in an increasing order of their existence since formation: A. Rajasthan Marudhara Gramin Bank B. Telangana Gramin Bank C. Saurashtra Gramin Bank D. Madhyanchal Gramin Bank E. Arunachal Pradesh Rural Bank
questions.note: Establishment years of these specific RRBs could not be verified with confidence; scan is also faint here. Verify against official key.

questions.question: Which of the following factors are associated with weakening of Indian rupee? A. Rupee payment for international trade B. Rising cost of imports C. Widening trade deficit D. Opening of Rupee Vostro accounts E. Rupee UPI payment for overseas transactions
questions.note: Rising cost of imports (B) and widening trade deficit (C) are clear drivers of rupee weakness; rupee payment for trade, Vostro accounts, and UPI for overseas transactions instead support/internationalize the rupee. Exact option lettering is uncertain from the scan; verify against official key.

questions.question: Arrange the steps in the book building process for pricing an issue of shares in India: A. Determine issue price, market clearing price and price discovery B. Book runner and syndicate members generate awareness, create demand and run the order book C. Appointment of the merchant banker and syndicate members (SEBI-registered intermediaries/underwriters) D. Preparation and filing of red herring prospectus with the SEBI for approval E. Allotment and listing of shares on stock exchange(s)
questions.note: Logical order: appoint merchant banker/underwriters -> file the red herring prospectus with SEBI -> book building/demand generation -> price discovery -> allotment and listing.

questions.question: Which of the following are functions of the Reserve Bank of India? A. Bank of Issue B. Banker's bank and lender of the last resort C. Regulator of fiscal policy D. Controller of credit E. Custodian of foreign exchange reserves

options.a: A, B, C and D only
options.b: A, B, D and E only
options.c: B, C, D and E only

questions.note: RBI is Bank of Issue, banker's bank/lender of last resort, controller of credit, and custodian of forex reserves; it is not a regulator of fiscal policy (that is the government's domain — RBI regulates monetary policy).

questions.question: The following legislations in primary and secondary market in ascending order of its enactment: A. Mutual fund regulations B. Credit rating agencies Regulations C. Credit rating regulations D. SEBI intermediaries regulations E. Sweat equity regulations
questions.note: Option lettering is faint in the scan; verify against official key.

questions.question: Which are correct regulatory provisions for foreign bank operations in India? A. They are incorporated in India and have their head office in a foreign country B. Foreign banks since 2012 have been allowed to set up their subsidiaries in India C. The foreign banks are allowed to operate in India even if they are not financially sound D. They have to operate according to the banking regulations in India E. RBI approved that foreign banks which are present in India could open their branches
questions.note: Foreign banks may set up wholly-owned subsidiaries in India (from 2013 guidelines), must comply with Indian banking regulations, and RBI approves branch expansion; they must be financially sound (C is false).

questions.question: Which one of the following subsidiaries is NOT owned by the Reserve Bank of India?

options.c: National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD)
options.d: Deposit Insurance and Credit Guarantee Corporation of India (DICGC)

questions.note: IDFC was never an RBI subsidiary. (NABARD's and NHB's RBI shareholding was also transferred to the Government over time, but among these options IDFC is the clear non-RBI entity.)

questions.question: Which one of the following is an operational technique of hedging transaction exposure?
questions.note: A mark in the source suggests option (d); note that (a),(b),(c) are also standard hedging techniques, so this may be a 'choose the odd one out' framing — verify wording against official key.

questions.question: Growing financial stress endangering economic stability in developed economies is the immediate consequence of which of the following?
questions.note: A mark in the source indicates option (d).

questions.question: 'Category I' companies (as classified by SEBI in this context) are:

options.a: Existing listed companies making a public issue
options.b: New companies with less than 12 months in operation
options.c: Companies having a good track record of profit

questions.note: Best inference from context; exact wording is faint in the scan — verify against official key.

questions.question: Which one of the following is concerned with Endowment Policy?

options.a: The insurer has the advantage of receiving money at regular intervals of the policy with a specific sum of money at the expiry of the policy
options.b: At the expiry of the policy, the insured receives the sum of the insurance policy
options.c: It covers the insured for the whole life; his nominee receives the assured sum with bonus after the death of the insured
options.d: The premium cost is high; if the insurer dies, the nominee receives the insurance amount

questions.note: An endowment policy pays the sum assured either at maturity (expiry of the term) or on earlier death.

questions.question: What are the positive attributes of mobile banking? A. Negative experience in European countries B. Wireless Application Protocol (WAP) C. Advanced Penetration of Mobile network D. Less security E. Faster data processing speed
questions.note: WAP enablement, advanced mobile penetration, and faster data processing are positive attributes; negative European experience and less security are negatives.

questions.question: Which of the following are considered as off-balance-sheet activities of a commercial Bank? A. Lending money to a depositor B. Borrowing from RBI C. Purchasing a futures contract D. Issuing letter of credit E. Engaging in a Swap Contract
questions.note: Futures contracts, letters of credit, and swap contracts are classic off-balance-sheet items; lending and borrowing appear on the balance sheet.

questions.question: Match List-I with List-II: List-I Committee: A. Bagri Committee B. Raghuram Rajan Committee C. Vaghul Committee D. Urjit Patel Committee / List-II Purpose: I. India's Money Market II. Reforms for Financial sector III. Supervision of Bank IV. Examining the monetary framework
questions.note: Vaghul Committee shaped India's money market (I), Raghuram Rajan Committee addressed financial sector reforms (II), Urjit Patel Committee examined the monetary policy framework (IV), leaving Bagri Committee with bank supervision (III).

questions.question: The coexistence and cooperation between the formal and informal financial sector is commonly referred to as:

options.d: Catering the financial needs of modern economy

questions.note: 'Financial dualism' is the standard term for coexistence of formal and informal finance.

questions.question: As the economy weakens, one would expect investment of funds in _____ to increase and investment in _____ funds to decrease.
questions.note: Question stem and options are faint/partial in the scan; verify against official key.

Expert group on foreign exchange markets / List-II Year: I. Rashid Jilani Committee (1992) II. Sodhani Committee (1994) III. Marathe Committee (1991) IV. Shere Committee (1995)

list_1.A: Study of all aspects of Electronic fund transfer (EFT)
list_1.D: Expert group on foreign exchange markets

questions.note: Committee-purpose mapping and lettering are not fully legible in the scan; verify against official key.

questions.question: Sequence the following steps in the operational functioning of Asset Reconstruction Companies as per the SARFAESI Act, 2002: A. Charge a 2 percent management fee B. Issue security receipts to bank C. Make payment to bank D. Buys loans of bank at a discount E. Carry out the recovery
questions.note: Logical process order should be: buy loans at a discount (D) -> make payment to the bank (C) -> issue security receipts (B) -> charge management fee (A) -> carry out recovery (E); this does not exactly match any transcribed option, so the option lettering here is uncertain. Verify against official key.

questions.question: Starting from the earliest, sequence the steps taken to develop the money market in India: A. Introduction of Interest Rate Swaps (IRSs) B. Introduction of Commercial Paper C. Introduction of Ways and Means Advances (WMA) linked to bank rate D. Introduction of Liquidity Adjustment Facility (LAF) E. Implementation of Real Time Gross Settlement (RTGS)
questions.note: Commercial Paper was introduced 1990, WMA linked to Bank Rate in 1997, Interest Rate Swaps permitted 1999, LAF introduced 1999-2000, and RTGS implemented 2004.

questions.question: The Directorate General of Foreign Trade (DGFT) facilitates and promotes foreign trade in India and also implements the foreign trade policy of India. Which of the following union ministries governs the DGFT?
questions.note: DGFT operates under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry.

questions.question: From the following, which is an uncommon feature of Private Equity and Venture Capital?

options.a: Both invest in companies that are not able to or ready to gain capital from the public
options.b: Their investment is used for financial or operating restructuring of the investee companies
options.c: They are set up as independent pools of capital contributed by institutions or high net worth individuals
options.d: Their activities are subject to few regulations

questions.note: Using investment for financial/operating restructuring of mature firms is characteristic of Private Equity, distinguishing it from Venture Capital (which funds early-stage growth) — making it the 'uncommon' (non-shared) feature.

questions.question: In the context of banking sector, Spread is defined as a function of:
questions.note: Spread (the gap between interest earned and interest paid) is closely tied to a bank's Net Interest Income.

questions.question: Which are the RBI notified domestic accredited credit rating agencies? A. Brickwork ratings B. Active ratings C. CRISIL ratings D. Standard and Poor's E. Moody's
questions.note: Brickwork Ratings and CRISIL are RBI-accredited domestic credit rating agencies; S&P and Moody's are international agencies.

questions.question: Which is the legal framework governing Regional Rural Banks (RRBs)? A. Regional Rural Banks Act, 1976 B. Regional Rural Banks Act, 1966 C. Small Industries Development Bank of India Act, 1949 D. Banking Regulation Act, 1949 E. Indian Partnership Act, 1932
questions.note: RRBs are governed by the Regional Rural Banks Act, 1976, and (like other banks) by the Banking Regulation Act, 1949.

questions.question: Which one of the following is a fully owned subsidiary of the RBI?

options.c: Indian Institute of Banking and Finance (IIBF)
options.d: Indian Financial Technology and Allied Services (IFTAS)

questions.note: IFTAS is a wholly-owned RBI subsidiary set up for IT/technology services to the banking sector.

questions.question: Which committee had recommended a comprehensive framework of reform in the insurance sector?
questions.note: The Malhotra Committee (1993) recommended comprehensive insurance sector reforms.

questions.question: Which of the following are the functions of Reserve Bank of India? A. Issue of Currency B. Accepting Deposits C. Banker to Government D. Credit Control
questions.note: RBI's core functions among these include issue of currency (A), banker to government (C), and credit control (D); accepting public deposits (B) is a commercial-bank function, not RBI's. The exact intended two-item combination in the source is unclear (A,C,D are all legitimate RBI functions); verify against official key.

questions.question: Which of the following are the advantages of Mobile Banking? A. Insecure B. Fraud reduction C. Time saving D. Separate internet required E. Increased efficiency
questions.note: Fraud reduction, time saving, and increased efficiency are advantages; insecurity and needing separate internet access are drawbacks/requirements, not advantages.

questions.question: Average clause in insurance is applicable for which one of the following cases?
questions.note: The 'average clause' applies in cases of under-insurance, proportionately reducing the claim payout.

questions.question: For ongoing maintenance of regulatory capital, which of the following risks were covered by Pillar-1 Minimum Capital Requirement? A. Credit Risk B. Financial risk C. Operation Risk D. Market Risk E. Reputational Risk
questions.note: Basel's Pillar 1 (Minimum Capital Requirements) covers Credit Risk, Operational Risk, and Market Risk.

questions.question: When the Central Bank conducts a sale of securities, the cash reserve of commercial banks shall:
questions.note: Open market sale of securities by the central bank absorbs liquidity, decreasing commercial banks' cash reserves.

questions.question: According to FEMA, foreign exchange does not include which one of the following?

options.a: Deposit payable in any foreign currency
options.b: Bills of exchange drawn in Indian currency but payable in any foreign currency
options.c: Traveller's cheques drawn by institutions outside India but payable in Indian currency
options.d: Draft drawn by banks outside India and payable in Indian currency

questions.note: A mark in the source indicates option (d).

questions.question: Which of the following are subsidiaries of RBI? A. National Housing Bank (NHB) B. National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD) C. Export Import Bank (EXIM Bank) D. Deposit Insurance and Credit Guarantee Corporation of India (DICGC) E. Bhartiya Reserve Bank Note Mudran Private Limited (BRBNMPL)
questions.note: DICGC and BRBNMPL are current wholly-owned RBI subsidiaries (RBI's shareholding in NHB and NABARD has since been transferred to the Government, and EXIM Bank was never RBI-owned).

questions.question: The Central Bank can significantly influence the savings, investments, and consumer spending in the economy through which one of the following policies?
questions.note: Monetary policy (interest rates, money supply) is the central bank's main lever affecting savings, investment, and spending.

questions.question: Which of the following statement(s) are correct? A. Asset liability management is a mechanism to address the risk arising due to mismatch of assets and liabilities B. Non-performing Assets (NPA) must be written off as loss in the financial year in which the NPA has been identified
questions.note: Statement A correctly defines Asset-Liability Management. Statement B is false — NPAs are classified through stages (sub-standard, doubtful, loss) rather than being automatically written off the year they're identified.

questions.question: Banker's sale of a mortgage portfolio by setting up mortgage pass-through securities is an example of:
questions.note: Pooling and selling mortgages via pass-through securities is the classic example of securitization.

questions.question: Why do Central banks intervene to affect exchange rates? A. To influence domestic production B. To influence trade flows C. To influence domestic interest rates D. To inject liquidity in domestic markets E. To smoothen fluctuations in exchange rates
questions.note: Central bank forex intervention is generally aimed at influencing domestic production/trade competitiveness (via trade flows) and smoothing exchange rate volatility.

questions.question: Which one of the following is an example of Secondary Reserves?

options.a: Cash in hand and balances with other banks in current accounts
options.d: Investment in Government Securities for SLR

questions.note: Secondary reserves are liquid, income-earning assets (like commercial paper/T-bills) held beyond mandatory cash reserves.

questions.question: If the subject matter of insurance is the ship, the marine insurance is called:
questions.note: Insurance on the ship itself is Hull insurance (as opposed to Cargo insurance for goods carried).

questions.question: A spot sale of a currency combined with a forward repurchase of the same currency is called which one of the following?
questions.note: Combining a spot transaction with an offsetting forward transaction in the same currency defines a forex swap.

questions.question: Which one of the following is a myth about rural markets?

options.a: All villages are not equally populated
options.b: Rural buyers are a heterogeneous lot
options.c: Rural buyers are able to discriminate between products and brands
options.d: Only low-priced products sell in rural markets

questions.note: 'Only low-priced products sell in rural markets' is the commonly cited myth — rural buyers do buy premium/branded products too.

questions.question: Match List-I with List-II (partially legible in the scan — table continues onto the next page)
questions.note: This question's table spans a page break in the scan and could not be reliably transcribed. Verify against the original source.

questions.question: Pricing of housing loan by a commercial bank may follow the following steps in a logical sequence: A. Competitive price determination B. Specification of spread C. Application of MCLR D. Conduct of Credit Assessment E. Quoting to prospective borrower
questions.note: Logical order: conduct credit assessment -> apply MCLR -> specify the spread -> arrive at the competitive price -> quote it to the borrower.

questions.question: The banks wherein a majority of depositors are non-residents are called:
